hypotheses.hypothesis: Evidence-based practice in psychology is too narrowly rooted in RCT ideals from physics and should embrace methodological pluralism
hypotheses.result: Argued philosophically; not empirically tested

title: Impact of fabrication history induced disorder on Josephson junction reproducibility and qubit performance
task: Understanding Josephson junction reproducibility and barrier disorder effects
key_results: Normal-state resistance variability governed by fabrication-history-induced disorder rather than oxide thickness; wafer-to-wafer reproducibility strongly affected by prior process steps
comments: Critical for scalable quantum processors; AFM and TEM data convincingly link surface roughness to barrier quality, though mechanisms at atomic scale remain partially opaque.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Oxide thickness is the primary determinant of JJ resistance
hypotheses.result: Rejected; fabrication-induced barrier disorder shown to dominate

hypotheses.hypothesis: Plasma-damaged surfaces produce higher resistance
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; nanoscale disorder rather than thickness causes effect

title: Opposite pressure effects on magnetic phase transitions in NiBr2
task: Pressure-induced magnetic phase transitions in NiBr₂
key_results: Collinear AFM Néel temperature increases ~20 K/GPa to ~100 K at 3 GPa; helical phase suppressed above ~0.8 GPa; opposite pressure behavior compared to NiI₂
comments: Ab initio calculations identify j₂′ as key driver, but the contrasting behavior with NiI₂ suggests subtle interplay between competing interlayer interactions.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Interlayer exchange j₂′ governs pressure response of collinear AFM in NiBr₂
hypotheses.result: Confirmed via ab initio calculations

hypotheses.hypothesis: In-plane exchange ratio makes helical order fragile in NiBr₂ vs NiI₂
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; helical phase suppressed at ~0.8 GPa in NiBr₂ vs stabilized to ~6 GPa in NiI₂
